assessment: Independent locator review confirms that only the identical-ion branch has a source-reported quantitative inversion-rate relation over alpha. The isotope-substituted branch reports qualitative locking at alpha approximately 1.09 and a numerical activation barrier, but no inversion-rate formula over a shared alpha domain. The ScienceCard assessment is internally contradictory: its opening claims two quantitative inversion-rate formulas and immediately states that the isotope branch lacks one. This card must not be approved for matched case authoring.

issues.detail: The identical-ion branch has a quantitative Kramers-Langer inversion-rate relation, but the isotope-substituted branch supplies only qualitative suppression and a barrier value, not a second source-reported inversion-rate formula.

The identical-ion rate claim is supported in the 1.05 < alpha < 1.29 bistable interval, whereas isotope suppression is reported only near alpha 1.09 and the isotope equilibrium-configuration discussion gives different pyramid thresholds; the source does not report a paired quantitative rate law on one shared alpha query domain.

The identical-ion quantitative observable is inversion rate extracted from dwell-time histograms, while the isotope quantitative value is a cNEB activation barrier. These are not the same operational readout.

The ScienceCard assessment first asserts two quantitative inversion-rate formulas, then states that the isotope-substituted cluster has no rate formula. The cited source supports the latter statement, so the card must not be approved.

review_material.assessment: The source provides two quantitative inversion-rate formulas for the identical-ion and isotope-substituted clusters, but the isotope-substituted cluster lacks a reported numeric inversion rate formula over a shared alpha domain. The identical-ion cluster has a K-L rate formula with fitted temperature and background rate, and the isotope-substituted cluster has a reported activation barrier of ~270 mK at alpha ~1.09, but no rate formula. Thus, the hinted cluster is partially supported; case_authoring_ready is false because no numeric control domain is shared between the two branches.

source_ambiguities.statement: The isotope-substituted cluster has a different alpha domain for pyramidal configurations (alpha > ~1.35 for global minimum) compared to the identical-ion cluster (1.05 < alpha < 1.29), and the suppression is observed at alpha ~ 1.09, which is outside the reported global minimum range for the isotope-substituted cluster. This may indicate a local minimum or metastable state.
